```{r, load_libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=TRUE, results='hide'}
##' Package Management:

# Function to check and install packages if they're not already installed
load_packages <- function(packages) {
  # Check which packages are not installed
  not_installed <- packages[!(packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
  
  # Install missing packages
  if(length(not_installed) > 0) {
    message("Installing missing packages: ", paste(not_installed, collapse = ", "))
    install.packages(not_installed, repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
  }
  
  # Load all packages
  for(pkg in packages) {
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    message(paste("Loaded package:", pkg))
  }
}

# List of required packages for the analysis
required_packages <- c(
"tidyverse",     # Core data science packages: ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, readr, purrr
"caret",         # Unified interface to train models and use resampling
"cluster",       # Clustering algorithms and silhouette width
"factoextra",    # Visualize clustering results beautifully
"dendextend",    # Dendrogram enhancement for hierarchical clustering
"clue",          # Tools for comparing clustering solutions
"kableExtra",    # Better tables in RMarkdown
"gridExtra",     # Arrange multiple ggplot2 plots
"dbscan",        # Density-based clustering
"knitr",         # For table formatting
"class",         # For classification methods in KNN
"gridExtra",     # arrange multiple grid-based plots
"lintr",         # code style and best practices and consistent styling
"pROC",          # Display and Analyze ROC Curves
"scales",        # Scale Functions for Visualization
"data.table",    # For efficient data handling
"readr",         # For reading CSV files
"kknn")          # Weighted k-Nearest Neighbors

# Load all required packages
load_packages(required_packages)

# Note: GAI was used on the coding, plotting and debugging part.
# The majority of the structure, data clean and modeling came from our workshops.
```

# Data Loading and Preprocessing
```{r data_loading, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}

read_csv("data/adult_train.csv")
read_csv("data/adult_test.csv")

# Define column names based on the dataset description
column_names <- c("age", "workclass", "fnlwgt", "education", "education_num", 
                 "marital_status", "occupation", "relationship", "race", 
                 "sex", "capital_gain", "capital_loss", "hours_per_week", 
                 "native_country", "income")

# Read training data with proper column names
train_data <- read_csv("data/adult_train.csv", 
                      col_names = column_names, 
                      trim_ws = TRUE, 
                      na = c("", "NA", "?", " ?"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

# The test file has a header row to remove
test_data <- readLines("data/adult_test.csv")

# Skip the first line (header) and write to a temporary file
# writeLines(test_data[-1], "data/bank_analysis/adult_test.csv")

# Read TEST data with proper column names
test_data <- read_csv("data/bank_analysis/adult_test.csv", 
                      col_names = column_names, 
                      trim_ws = TRUE, 
                      na = c("", "NA", "?", " ?"),  
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

# Fix the income column in test data (it has a period at the end)
test_data$income <- gsub("\\.", "", test_data$income)

# Check dimensions of both datasets
cat("Training data dimensions:", dim(train_data)[1], "rows,", dim(train_data)[2], "columns\n")
cat("Test data dimensions:", dim(test_data)[1], "rows,", dim(test_data)[2], "columns\n")
```

```{r preprocessing, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# Data preprocessing steps
# Check the structure of both datasets
str(train_data)
str(test_data)

# Combine datasets for consistent preprocessing
# Add a column to identify the source
train_data$source <- "train"
test_data$source <- "test"
combined_data <- rbind(train_data, test_data)

# Clean up the income variable (remove spaces and periods)
combined_data$income <- gsub(" ", "", combined_data$income)
combined_data$income <- gsub("\\.", "", combined_data$income)

# Convert income to a factor with consistent levels
combined_data$income <- factor(combined_data$income, 
                               levels = c("<=50K", ">50K"))

# Handle missing values (marked as "?")
# For factor variables: replace "?" with "Unknown"
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, function(x) ifelse(x == "?", "Unknown", x))

# Identify numeric columns
numeric_cols <- c("age", "fnlwgt", "education_num", "capital_gain", 
                 "capital_loss", "hours_per_week")

# For numeric columns, replace "?" with NA
for (col in numeric_cols) {
  combined_data[[col]] <- as.numeric(as.character(combined_data[[col]]))
}

# Remove rows with NA values - following the workshop practice
combined_data <- na.omit(combined_data)

# Convert character columns to factors
combined_data <- combined_data %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)

# Normalize numeric variables (following Workshop 9 example)
normalize <- function(x) { (x-min(x)) / (max(x)-min(x)) }

# Identify numeric columns (excluding source which is our identifier)
numeric_cols <- c("age", "fnlwgt", "education_num", "capital_gain", 
                 "capital_loss", "hours_per_week")

# Normalize numeric columns
combined_data[numeric_cols] <- lapply(combined_data[numeric_cols], normalize)

# Split back into train and test datasets
train_clean <- combined_data %>% filter(source == "train") %>% select(-source)
test_clean <- combined_data %>% filter(source == "test") %>% select(-source)

# Verify the distribution of income in both datasets
summary(train_clean$income)/nrow(train_clean)
summary(test_clean$income)/nrow(test_clean)

# Look for any remaining issues
anyNA(train_clean)
anyNA(test_clean)

# Save the cleaned datasets
write.csv(train_clean, "train_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(test_clean, "test_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create datasets for clustering (without income column)
train_cluster <- train_clean %>% select(-income)
test_cluster <- test_clean %>% select(-income)

# Save datasets ready for clustering
write.csv(train_cluster, "train_cluster.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(test_cluster, "test_cluster.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## KNN Classifications 
```{r 1st_knn, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# KNN Classification Model
# -------------------------
# Sample the data for efficiency
# Set a seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)
train_sample <- train_clean %>% 
  sample_frac(0.50)  # Use 50% of the training data for initial models

# KNN Model 1: Basic KNN with default parameters
set.seed(123)
knn_model1 <- train(
  form = income ~ .,
  data = train_sample,
  method = 'knn',
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = 'cv',
    number = 5,
    verboseIter = TRUE
  )
)

# View model results
print(knn_model1)
plot(knn_model1)
# Following Workshop 9 examples to build and evaluate KNN models

```

```{r 2nd_knn, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# KNN Model 2: KNN with expanded k values 
# -------------------------
# Set a seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)
knn_model2 <- train(
  form = income ~ .,
  data = train_sample,
  method = 'knn',
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(.k = seq(5, 25, by = 2)),  # Odd k values from 5 to 25
  metric = 'Accuracy',
  trControl = trainControl(
    method = 'cv',
    number = 5,
    verboseIter = TRUE
  )
)

# View results
print(knn_model2)
plot(knn_model2)
```

```{r knn_sum_table, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='always'}
# Evaluate all models on test set
# Create function to evaluate models
evaluate_model <- function(model, test_data, model_name, accuracy_label) {
  # Predict on test data
  predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)
  
  # Calculate confusion matrix
  cm <- confusionMatrix(predictions, test_data$income, positive = ">50K")
  
  # Extract metrics
  accuracy <- cm$overall["Accuracy"]
  precision <- cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]
  recall <- cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  
  # Get best k value directly from the final model
  best_k <- model$finalModel$k
  
  # Return as data frame row
  data.frame(
    AccuracyLabel = accuracy_label,
    Model = model_name,
    Best_k = best_k,
    Accuracy = accuracy,
    Precision = precision,
    Recall = recall
  )
}

# List of models, names and accuracy labels
models <- list(knn_model1, knn_model2, knn_model3, knn_model4, knn_model5)
model_names <- c("Basic KNN", "Extended value KNN", "KNN with preprocessing Center and scale", 
                "Recall KNN", "Weighted KNN")
accuracy_labels <- c("Accuracy1", "Accuracy2", "Accuracy3", "Accuracy4", "Accuracy5")

# Evaluate each model
results_list <- lapply(1:length(models), function(i) {
  evaluate_model(models[[i]], test_clean, model_names[i], accuracy_labels[i])
})

# Combine results
knn_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

# Create a table for report
knn_results_table <- knn_results %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 4))) %>%
  arrange(desc(Accuracy))

# Print formatted table
kable(knn_results_table, 
      caption = "KNN Model Performance Comparison", 
      format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

```{r knn_comparison_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
# Create long format data for plotting
plot_data <- knn_results %>%
  select(Model, Accuracy, Precision, Recall) %>%
  gather(key = "Metric", value = "Value", -Model) %>%
  mutate(
    Value = round(Value, 4),
    Model = factor(Model, levels = model_names)
  )

# Create the comparison plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Model, y = Value, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", Value)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "KNN Models Performance Comparison",
    x = "Model Type",
    y = "Score",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    legend.position = "top"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  ylim(0, max(plot_data$Value) + 0.1)  # Add some space for the labels

# Add a horizontal line at the best accuracy
best_accuracy <- max(knn_results$Accuracy)
best_model <- knn_results$Model[which.max(knn_results$Accuracy)]

cat("\nBest performing model:", best_model, "with accuracy:", round(best_accuracy, 4))
```


```{r k_comparison, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, echo=FALSE, eval=params$report_type == "management", echo=FALSE, results='always'}
# Extract k values and accuracies from each model's tuning results
plot_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    Model = "Basic KNN",
    k = knn_model1$results$k,
    Accuracy = knn_model1$results$Accuracy
  ),
  data.frame(
    Model = "Extended value KNN",
    k = knn_model2$results$k,
    Accuracy = knn_model2$results$Accuracy
  ),
  data.frame(
    Model = "KNN with preprocessing",
    k = knn_model3$results$k,
    Accuracy = knn_model3$results$Accuracy
  ),
  data.frame(
    Model = "Recall KNN",
    k = knn_model4$results$k,
    Accuracy = knn_model4$results$Accuracy
  ),
  data.frame(
    Model = "Weighted KNN",
    k = knn_model5$results$k,
    Accuracy = knn_model5$results$Accuracy
  )
)

# Create the line plot with improved visibility
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = k, y = Accuracy, color = Model)) +
  # Add background grid for readability
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq(min(plot_data$Accuracy, na.rm = TRUE), 
                              max(plot_data$Accuracy, na.rm = TRUE), 
                              by = 0.005), 
             color = "gray90", linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Add thicker lines for better visibility
  geom_line(size = 1.5) +
  
  # Make the weighted KNN line even thicker and brighter red
  geom_line(data = plot_data %>% filter(Model == "Weighted KNN"),
            aes(x = k, y = Accuracy),
            color = "#FF0000", size = 2.5) +
  
  # Add larger points
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.9) +
  
  # Highlight optimal k points with larger circles
  geom_point(data = plot_data %>% 
               group_by(Model) %>% 
               filter(Accuracy == max(Accuracy)),
             aes(x = k, y = Accuracy), 
             size = 7, shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "black", stroke = 1.5) +
  
  # Add text annotations for best k values with improved visibility and positioning
  geom_label(data = plot_data %>% 
              group_by(Model) %>% 
              filter(Accuracy == max(Accuracy)),
            aes(label = sprintf("k=%d\nAcc=%.3f", k, Accuracy),
                fill = Model),
            vjust = -1.5, hjust = 0.5,
            size = 4, fontface = "bold",
            color = "black",
            alpha = 0.9,
            label.padding = unit(0.5, "lines"),
            label.size = 0.5) +
  
  # Improved titles and labels with larger font
  labs(
    title = "KNN Model Performance Comparison Across Different k Values",
    subtitle = "Comparison of five different KNN implementations with optimal k values highlighted",
    x = "Number of Neighbors (k)",
    y = "Cross-Validation Accuracy",
    color = "Model Type",
    fill = "Model Type"
  ) +
  
  # Use a clean theme with improved aesthetics and larger fonts
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, color = "gray30"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.5, "cm"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray80", fill = NA, size = 1)
  ) +
  
  # Custom color palette with brighter colors for better visibility
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#1E90FF", "#00CD66", "#9932CC", "#FFA500", "#FF0000")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#1E90FF", "#00CD66", "#9932CC", "#FFA500", "#FF0000"),
                   guide = "none") +
  
  # Ensure y-axis shows enough precision
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.001),
                    limits = c(min(plot_data$Accuracy) - 0.002, 
                              max(plot_data$Accuracy) + 0.005))
```

```{r clustering_data_prep, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' Clustering Data Preparation 
# -------------------------
##' Determine optimal number of clusters for different approaches
# Prepare data for clustering (exclude income for unbiased clustering)
set.seed(123)
train_sample_cluster <- train_sample %>% select(-income)
train_sample_with_income <- train_sample # Keep a copy with income for later analysis

# Get only numeric features and handle missing values
train_numeric <- train_sample_cluster %>% 
  select_if(is.numeric) %>%
  # Replace NA values with column means
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .)))

# Check dimensions
cat("Dimensions after handling missing values:\n")
cat("train_numeric:", dim(train_numeric), "\n")
cat("train_sample_with_income:", dim(train_sample_with_income), "\n")

# For subset of features
numeric_features <- c("age", "education_num", "capital_gain", "hours_per_week")
train_subset <- train_sample_cluster[numeric_features] %>%
  # Replace NA values with column means
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(is.na(.), mean(., na.rm = TRUE), .)))
```

```{r knn1, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
cat("Income length:", length(train_sample_with_income$income), "\n")
```

```{r knn4, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' MODEL 4: PAM (Partitioning Around Medoids) with K=5
# -------------------------
set.seed(123)
pam_model <- pam(train_numeric, k = optimal_k_all, diss = FALSE)

# Create contingency table
model4_table <- table(Cluster = pam_model$clustering, Income = train_sample_with_income$income)
print(model4_table)

# Calculate percentages
model4_percentages <- prop.table(model4_table, margin = 1) * 100
print(model4_percentages)
```

```{r knn5, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' MODEL 5: Hierarchical Clustering with K=5
# -------------------------
# Compute distance matrix
dist_matrix <- dist(train_numeric, method = "euclidean")

# Perform hierarchical clustering
hclust_model <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "ward.D2")

# Cut the tree to get optimal number of clusters
hclust_clusters <- cutree(hclust_model, k = optimal_k_all)

# Create contingency table
model5_table <- table(Cluster = hclust_clusters, Income = train_sample_with_income$income)
print(model5_table)

# Calculate percentages
model5_percentages <- prop.table(model5_table, margin = 1) * 100
print(model5_percentages)
```

```{r knn_all_compare, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' Compare All Clustering Models
# -------------------------
# Create a function to calculate silhouette score
calculate_silhouette <- function(data, cluster_assignments) {
  sil <- silhouette(cluster_assignments, dist(data))
  mean(sil[,3])  # Average silhouette width
}

# Calculate silhouette scores for each model
silhouette_scores <- data.frame(
  Model = c("K-means (K=5)", "K-means (K=3)", "K-means Selected Features (K=4)", 
            "PAM (K=5)", "Hierarchical (K=5)"),
  Silhouette_Score = c(
    calculate_silhouette(train_numeric, kmeans_model1$cluster),
    calculate_silhouette(train_numeric, kmeans_model2$cluster),
    calculate_silhouette(train_subset, kmeans_model3$cluster),
    calculate_silhouette(train_numeric, pam_model$clustering),
    calculate_silhouette(train_numeric, hclust_clusters)
  )
)

# Sort by silhouette score (higher is better)
silhouette_scores <- silhouette_scores[order(-silhouette_scores$Silhouette_Score),]
print(silhouette_scores)
```

```{r cluster_income_vize,eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' Visualize Income Distribution by Cluster for Each Model
# -------------------------
# Function to create income distribution visualizations
plot_income_distribution <- function(clusters, income_data, model_name) {
  cluster_data <- data.frame(
    Cluster = as.factor(clusters),
    Income = income_data
  )
  
  ggplot(cluster_data, aes(x = Cluster, fill = Income)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(title = paste("Income Distribution by Cluster -", model_name),
         x = "Cluster",
         y = "Percentage",
         fill = "Income") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Create visualization for each model
plot1 <- plot_income_distribution(kmeans_model1$cluster, train_sample_with_income$income, "K-means (K=3)")
plot2 <- plot_income_distribution(kmeans_model2$cluster, train_sample_with_income$income, "K-means (K=5)")
plot3 <- plot_income_distribution(kmeans_model3$cluster, train_sample_with_income$income, "K-means Selected Features (K=3)")
plot4 <- plot_income_distribution(pam_model$clustering, train_sample_with_income$income, "PAM (K=3)")
plot5 <- plot_income_distribution(hclust_clusters, train_sample_with_income$income, "Hierarchical (K=3)")

# Display all plots in a grid
grid.arrange(plot1, plot2, plot3, plot4, plot5, ncol = 2)
```

```{r cluster_best_model, eval=params$report_type == "technical", echo=TRUE, results='asis'}
##' Analyze Cluster Characteristics for the Best Model
# -------------------------
# Identify the best model based on silhouette score
best_model_name <- silhouette_scores$Model[1]
cat("The best clustering model based on silhouette score is:", best_model_name, "\n")

# Extract cluster assignments from the best model based on which has the highest score
if(best_model_name == "K-means (K=5)") {
  best_clusters <- kmeans_model1$cluster
  expected_clusters <- 5
  model_percentages <- model1_percentages
} else if(best_model_name == "K-means (K=3)") {
  best_clusters <- kmeans_model2$cluster
  expected_clusters <- 3
  model_percentages <- model2_percentages
} else if(best_model_name == "K-means Selected Features (K=4)") {
  best_clusters <- kmeans_model3$cluster
  expected_clusters <- 4
  model_percentages <- model3_percentages
} else if(best_model_name == "PAM (K=5)") {
  best_clusters <- pam_model$clustering
  expected_clusters <- 5
  model_percentages <- model4_percentages
} else if(best_model_name == "Hierarchical (K=5)") {
  best_clusters <- hclust_clusters
  expected_clusters <- 5
  model_percentages <- model5_percentages
}

# Verify all clusters are present
present_clusters <- sort(unique(best_clusters))
cat("\nExpected", expected_clusters, "clusters. Found", length(present_clusters), "clusters:", paste(present_clusters, collapse=", "), "\n")

# Check if any expected clusters are missing
if(length(present_clusters) < expected_clusters) {
  cat("WARNING: Some clusters are empty or missing. This can happen with certain data distributions.\n")
}

# Use the appropriate data for the best model
if(best_model_name == "K-means Selected Features (K=4)") {
  cluster_profile_data <- cbind(train_subset, Cluster = as.factor(best_clusters))
} else {
  cluster_profile_data <- cbind(train_numeric, Cluster = as.factor(best_clusters))
}

# Calculate mean values for each feature by cluster
cluster_profiles <- aggregate(. ~ Cluster, data = cluster_profile_data, mean)
print(cluster_profiles)

# Create a comprehensive cluster summary table
cluster_summary <- data.frame(
  Cluster = as.numeric(levels(as.factor(best_clusters))),
  Size = as.numeric(table(best_clusters)),
  Size_Percent = round(100 * as.numeric(table(best_clusters)) / length(best_clusters), 1)
)

# Add income percentages for each cluster
for(i in 1:nrow(cluster_summary)) {
  cluster_id <- cluster_summary$Cluster[i]
  if(as.character(cluster_id) %in% rownames(model_percentages)) {
    cluster_summary$HighIncome_Pct[i] <- round(model_percentages[as.character(cluster_id), ">50K"], 1)
  } else {
    cluster_summary$HighIncome_Pct[i] <- NA
  }
}

# Add descriptive labels based on feature profiles
# Match cluster numbers to cluster_profiles rows
cluster_summary$Education <- NA
cluster_summary$Age <- NA
cluster_summary$WorkHours <- NA
cluster_summary$CapitalGains <- NA

for(i in 1:nrow(cluster_summary)) {
  cluster_id <- cluster_summary$Cluster[i]
  # Find matching row in cluster_profiles
  profile_row <- which(cluster_profiles$Cluster == cluster_id)
  
  if(length(profile_row) > 0) {
    # Education level categorization
    edu_value <- cluster_profiles[profile_row, "education_num"]
    if(!is.na(edu_value)) {
      if(edu_value > 0.7) cluster_summary$Education[i] <- "High"
      else if(edu_value > 0.5) cluster_summary$Education[i] <- "Medium"
      else cluster_summary$Education[i] <- "Low"
    }
    
    # Age categorization
    age_value <- cluster_profiles[profile_row, "age"]
    if(!is.na(age_value)) {
      if(age_value > 0.4) cluster_summary$Age[i] <- "Older"
      else if(age_value > 0.25) cluster_summary$Age[i] <- "Middle-aged"
      else cluster_summary$Age[i] <- "Younger"
    }
    
    # Work hours categorization
    hours_value <- cluster_profiles[profile_row, "hours_per_week"]
    if(!is.na(hours_value)) {
      if(hours_value > 0.45) cluster_summary$WorkHours[i] <- "Long"
      else if(hours_value > 0.4) cluster_summary$WorkHours[i] <- "Average"
      else cluster_summary$WorkHours[i] <- "Short"
    }
    
    # Capital gains categorization
    capital_value <- cluster_profiles[profile_row, "capital_gain"]
    if(!is.na(capital_value)) {
      if(capital_value > 0.02) cluster_summary$CapitalGains[i] <- "High"
      else if(capital_value > 0.005) cluster_summary$CapitalGains[i] <- "Medium"
      else cluster_summary$CapitalGains[i] <- "Low"
    }
  }
}

# Sort by high income percentage (descending)
cluster_summary <- cluster_summary[order(-cluster_summary$HighIncome_Pct),]

# Add customer segment labels based on characteristics
cluster_summary$CustomerSegment <- paste0(
  "Segment ", 1:nrow(cluster_summary), ": ",
  cluster_summary$Age, " age, ",
  cluster_summary$Education, " education, ",
  cluster_summary$WorkHours, " hours"
)
# Print the comprehensive summary
cat("\n### Customer Segment Analysis Based on Clustering\n\n")
print(cluster_summary)

# Identify the highest-value cluster
highest_value_cluster <- cluster_summary$Cluster[1]  # Already sorted by HighIncome_Pct
highest_value_pct <- cluster_summary$HighIncome_Pct[1]

# Visualize feature profiles by cluster with better formatting
cluster_profiles_long <- reshape2::melt(cluster_profiles, id.vars = "Cluster")

# Create a more readable plot
ggplot(cluster_profiles_long, aes(x = variable, y = value, fill = Cluster)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = paste("Feature Profiles for", best_model_name),
       subtitle = paste("Comparing average feature values across", length(unique(best_clusters)), "customer segments"),
       x = "Feature",
       y = "Normalized Value (0-1 scale)",
       fill = "Cluster") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    legend.position = "top"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```
